# Create a design from scratch

A color and a personality picked from nothing is arbitrary, and looks it.
This skill grounds the choice in real products people already know, then
hands off to kx-design to build a system from it. It stops at the direction —
it does not produce tokens, CSS, or a palette.

## 1. Name the target, not the vibe

Two things, asked directly if the request didn't say them — an invented
personality is the exact failure mode this skill exists to avoid:

- **Category** — what kind of product this is: fintech, dev tool, consumer
  marketplace, AI platform, and so on.
- **2–4 personality words** — trustworthy, playful, serious, luxury, minimal,
  enterprise, editorial...

## 2. Find comparables, don't invent

[design.ricoui.com/brands](https://design.ricoui.com/brands) is a live
library of real brand design systems (Airbnb, Airtable, and dozens more),
each broken into an AI-extracted `DESIGN.md` — colors, type, a one-paragraph
rationale — read off the live site. It's a JS app: a plain fetch returns only
navigation chrome, confirmed in practice, so browse it with the
`agent-browser` skill rather than `WebFetch`.

```bash
agent-browser open https://design.ricoui.com/brands
agent-browser snapshot -i -c        # category and style-tag filters are buttons in the left rail
agent-browser click <category-or-tag-ref>   # narrow to the target's category and style
agent-browser snapshot -i -c        # read the filtered cards: name, one-line description, tags
```

Pick 2–3 candidates whose description and tags actually match the target —
not just the first cards on the page. Open each and read its **DESIGN.md**
tab specifically:

```bash
agent-browser click <brand-card-view-ref>
agent-browser snapshot -i -c        # DESIGN.md tab: rationale paragraph + color token table
```

Skip the Tailwind v4 / CSS Variables / Design Tokens tabs — same data in a
code format kx-design generates for itself once the base color is picked.

If `agent-browser` isn't available here, say so and ask the user to name 2–3
comparable brands directly, rather than guessing at what the site would have
shown.

## 3. Present, don't pick alone

Show the comparables with one line each: what fits, what doesn't, and why.
Let the user choose or synthesize — this is a brand decision, not a technical
one.

## 4. Hand off a direction, not a copy

State the outcome as:

- base color, converted to **HSL** — kx-design forbids hex
- the 2–4 personality words
- light or dark as the default stance

Never carry a comparable's tokens into the project wholesale. It's another
product's brand, and the site's own extraction is unverified against the live
source — its own pages say to "compare and validate." It's a reference point,
not a source.

Hand off explicitly: kx-design builds the actual scales — spacing, type, the
9-shade color ramp, hierarchy — from this base color and these words.
